name: Maqsum
desc: The most widely used iqa' in Arabic music, a versatile 4/4 cycle (DUM tak - tak DUM - tak) foundational to modern song, tarab and belly dance. Skeleton D-T-T-D--T on an eighth grid.
source: maqamworld.com/en/iqaa/maqsum.php; khafif.com/rhy [DT-TD-T-]; Carmine Guida Rhythm Cheat Sheet (Karim Nagi/Raquy/Jas)

name: Baladi (Masmudi Saghir)
desc: Earthy Egyptian folk 4/4 ('Little Masmudi'), distinguished from Maqsum by two leading DUMs (DUM DUM - tak DUM - tak). Heavy and grounded, ideal for hip drops.
source: maqamworld.com/en/iqaa/baladi.php; Carmine Guida Cheat Sheet 'Baladi (basic) D D _ T D _ T'; khafif.com/rhy

name: Saidi
desc: Upper-Egyptian 4/4 of the Maqsum family with two central DUMs (DUM tak - DUM DUM - tak), associated with cane (assaya) dance and saidi music.
source: maqamworld.com/en/iqaa/saidi.php; Carmine Guida Cheat Sheet 'Saidi (basic) D T _ D D _ T'; babayagamusic.com

name: Maqsum Maqluub (Saidi maqluub)
desc: 'Inverted' Maqsum/Saidi where the opening beat is played as a tak, dragging the accent onto the central double-DUM (tak tak - DUM DUM - tak). Common folk variation.
source: maqamworld.com/en/iqaa/saidi.php; khafif.com/rhy 'baladii maqluub'; Carmine Guida 'Saidi (variation) T D _ D D _ T'

name: Nawari
desc: Levantine 4/4 variation on Saidi/Baladi used in dabke line dances (tak DUM - tak DUM - tak); often called Katakufti by percussionists.
source: maqamworld.com/en/iqaa/nawari.php; Carmine Guida Cheat Sheet 'Nawari T D _ T D _ T'

name: Wahda
desc: 'The one' - a slow open 4/4 with a single DUM at the head of the bar and light taks filling the space, common in slow songs and taqasim accompaniment.
source: maqamworld.com/en/iqaa/wahda.php; Carmine Guida Cheat Sheet 'Wahda D _ _ T _ _ T'; mynoota.com/en/blog/iqaat

name: Wahda wa-Nuss (Wahda w-Nuss)
desc: 'One and a half' - a 4/4 elaboration of Wahda adding a second DUM on beat 3 (DUM - tak - DUM - tak), bridging Wahda and Maqsum feels.
source: maqamworld.com/en/iqaa.php (Wahda w-Nuss 4/4); babayagamusic.com

name: Wahda Kabira (Sayyah)
desc: 'Big Wahda' (Sayyah), an 8/4 cycle spread over two bars with sparse DUMs and taks; sensual and spacious, favored for taqsim improvisation.
source: maqamworld.com/en/iqaa.php (Wahda Kabira 8/4); babayagamusic.com 'Wahda Kebira'; mynoota.com/en/blog/iqaat

name: Masmudi Kabir (Masmoudi)
desc: 'Big Masmudi', a slow majestic 8/4 with two leading DUMs opening the cycle followed by taks (DUM - DUM - ... tak - tak); an art-music rhythm rooted in muwashahat.
source: maqamworld.com/en/iqaa/masmudi_kabir.php; Carmine Guida Cheat Sheet 'Masmoudi (basic) D _ D _ TK ...'; babayagamusic.com

name: Masmudi Kabir (3-DUM)
desc: Three-DUM variant of Masmudi Kabir adding a DUM on beat 3 of the first measure, giving a heavier 'warring/walking masmudi' stride for marching feels.
source: Carmine Guida Cheat Sheet '3 Doum Masmoudi has Doum on 3'; khafif.com/rhy 'warring/walking masmoudi'

name: Fallahi
desc: Fast Egyptian peasant 2/4 ('fellah' = farmer), essentially a brisk doubled Maqsum (DUM tak - tak DUM - tak) used for energetic hip lifts and shimmy walks.
source: maqamworld.com/en/iqaa/fallahi.php; babayagamusic.com 'Fellahi D t _ t D _ t'

name: Malfuf
desc: Fast 'wrapped' 2/4 (counted 3+3+2) used as an entrance/exit and intro rhythm: DUM - - tak - - tak. Light and rolling.
source: maqamworld.com/en/iqaa/malfuf.php; Carmine Guida Cheat Sheet 'Malfuf (basic) D _T _ T'; babayagamusic.com

name: Ayyub (Ayoub)
desc: Driving 2/4 zikr/trance rhythm (DUM - - DUM tak), said to evoke a walking camel; the backbone of Sufi and saidi-shaabi grooves.
source: maqamworld.com/en/iqaa/ayyub.php; Carmine Guida Cheat Sheet 'Ayub (basic) D _k D T'; babayagamusic.com

name: Karatshi (Karachi)
desc: Fast 2/4 that inverts Ayyub by swapping DUMs and taks (tak - - DUM DUM), giving an off-balance lift.
source: maqamworld.com/en/iqaa.php (Karachi 2/4); Carmine Guida Cheat Sheet 'Karachi (basic) T _k T D - inverted Ayub'

name: Khaleeji (Khaligi)
desc: Arabian-Gulf 2/4 (DUM - - DUM tak), described as Malfuf with two DUMs; underpins khaleegy hair-tossing dance and saudi/kuwaiti pop.
source: maqamworld.com/en/iqaa.php; Carmine Guida Cheat Sheet 'Khaligi (basic) D _D _ T - Malfuf with 2 Doums'; ancient-future.com

name: Wahda Saghira
desc: 'Small Wahda', a light 2/4 with a single DUM head and two taks (counted 3+3+2), close kin to Malfuf and used as a gentle filler groove.
source: maqamworld.com/en/iqaa.php (Wahda Saghira 2/4); khafif.com/rhy 'waaHida saghiira 3-3-2'

name: Fox (Rumba)
desc: Latin-influenced 2/4 ('Fox'/Rumba) absorbed into modern Arabic pop, with a syncopated DUM - - DUM tak - tak feel under foxtrot/rumba-style songs.
source: maqamworld.com/en/iqaa.php (Fox 2/4, Rumba 4/4); orientaldrumming.com

name: Zaffa
desc: Egyptian wedding-procession march in 4/4 with a dense tak roll between two strong DUMs (DUM tt t t DUM t t), used to announce the bridal party.
source: maqamworld.com/en/iqaa/zaffa.php; Carmine Guida Cheat Sheet 'Zaffa D tt t t D t t'; babayagamusic.com

name: Hacha
desc: A 4/4 iqa' in the maqsum/wahda family with DUMs on beats 1 and 3 and taks marking the off-beats, used in Egyptian folk and shaabi accompaniment.
source: maqamworld.com/en/iqaa.php (Hacha' 4/4); orientaldrumming.com

name: Bambi
desc: An 8/4 modern rhythm akin to a Wahda with a three-DUM cluster, played sparse and spacious (DUM kt -k t kt -k DUM DUM).
source: maqamworld.com/en/iqaa.php (Bambi 8/4); Carmine Guida Cheat Sheet 'Bambi D KT _K T KT _K D D'

name: Sombati
desc: A broad, dignified 8/4 of the maqsum family with widely spaced DUMs and syncopated taks, used to accompany slow tarab songs and entrances.
source: maqamworld.com/en/iqaa.php; Carmine Guida Cheat Sheet 'Sombati D kT _k T D kk T kk'; khafif.com/rhy

name: Ciftetelli (Chiftetelli)
desc: Slow, sensuous 8/4 (Turkish/Levantine) with a DUM-DUM-tak pull around beats 5-7 of the second bar; classic for veil work and taqsim improvisation.
source: maqamworld.com/en/iqaa.php (Ciftetelli 8/4); Carmine Guida Cheat Sheet 'Ciftetelli D _ K T _ K T / D _ D _ T'; suhaila.com/rhythms

name: Katakufti
desc: An 8/8 dabke-family iqa' with three opening DUMs and closing taks; when started from its last tak it sounds like Nawari.
source: maqamworld.com/en/iqaa/katakufti.php; maqamworld.com/en/iqaa/nawari.php (Katakufti relationship)

name: Sama'i Thaqil
desc: The principal 10/8 cycle of the Ottoman saz semai and Arabic muwashah, grouped 3+2+2+3 (DUM - - tak - DUM DUM - tak - tak), heavy and stately.
source: maqamworld.com/en/iqaa/samai_thaqil.php; dubsahara.wordpress.com/rhythms/10-8/samai; oudforguitarists.com (beats 1,4,6,7,8 emphasized)

name: Sama'i Darij
desc: A light, flowing 3/4 iqa' (DUM tak tak) used in both vocal and instrumental muwashah and as the fast final section of a sama'i.
source: maqamworld.com/en/iqaa/samai_darij.php; nesmaacademy.com Muwashahat Sama'i Darij

name: Sama'i Saraband
desc: A 3/8 muwashah iqa' (DUM - DUM - tak) related to the European sarabande, played with a dignified lilt in the vocal repertoire.
source: maqamworld.com/en/iqaa/samai_saraband.php; maqamworld.com/en/iqaa.php

name: Dawr Hindi
desc: 'Cycle of India', a 7/8 muwashah iqa' grouped 3+2+2 (DUM - tak DUM - tak), very popular in the vocal composed genre.
source: maqamworld.com/en/iqaa/dawr_hindi.php; dubsahara.wordpress.com/rhythms/7-8/dawr-hindi (7/8 = 3+2+2, D _ T D _ T)

name: Nawakht
desc: A mellow 7/4 muwashah iqa' with DUMs anchoring the cycle and taks on the off-pulses; played at a relaxed tempo in the muwashah repertoire.
source: maqamworld.com/en/iqaa/nawakht.php; maqamworld.com/en/iqaa.php (Nawakht 7/4)

name: Nawakht Hindi
desc: A long 16/4 muwashah cycle combining the Nawakht and Hindi feels, with DUM clusters and taks distributed across the extended bar.
source: maqamworld.com/en/iqaa/nawakht_hindi.php; maqamworld.com/en/iqaa.php (Nawakht Hindi 16/4)

name: Aqsaq (Aksak)
desc: 'Limping' 9/8 grouped 2+2+2+3, very popular in muwashah; an alternate form replaces the rest on beat 6 with a second DUM for two consecutive DUMs.
source: maqamworld.com/en/iqaa/aqsaq.php; maqamworld.com/en/iqaa.php (Aqsaq 9/8)

name: Thurayya (Aqsaq Turki)
desc: A 5/8 'Turkish aksak' iqa' grouped 2+3 (DUM - tak tak), a short limping cycle used in muwashah and Turkish-influenced pieces.
source: maqamworld.com/en/iqaa/thurayya.php; maqamworld.com/en/iqaa.php (Thurayya 5/8)

name: Jurjina (Curcuna)
desc: Iraqi/Kurdish/Turkish 10/8 cycle (counted 3+2+2+3 / 'Jorjuna'), DUM - - tak - DUM - tak, widely used in Iraqi maqam and folk dance.
source: maqamworld.com/en/iqaa/jurjina.php; Carmine Guida Cheat Sheet 'Curcuna (basic) D _ _ T _ D _ T' (10/8)

name: Yuruk Semai
desc: A brisk Turkish-origin 6/8 usul (DUM tak tak DUM tak) very popular in the muwashah genre as a fast closing rhythm.
source: maqamworld.com/en/iqaa/yuruk_semai.php; Carmine Guida Cheat Sheet 'York Semai D T T D T' (Karim Nagi)

name: Sudasi
desc: A 6/4 line-dance iqa' ('based on six') with a run of DUMs and a tak, used to accompany Lebanese and Palestinian dabke.
source: maqamworld.com/en/iqaa/sudasi.php; Carmine Guida Cheat Sheet 'Sudasi D _ D D _ D D _ T'

name: Mudawwar Masri
desc: Egyptian 'rounded' 12/4 muwashah iqa' with DUM anchors and taks across the long cycle; a stately art-music rhythm.
source: maqamworld.com/en/iqaa/mudawwar.php; maqamworld.com/en/iqaa.php (Mudawwar Masri 12/4)

name: Mudawwar Shami
desc: Damascene/pan-Syrian 'rounded' 10/4 form of Mudawwar used in the muwashah repertoire, with DUMs framing the cycle and taks between.
source: maqamworld.com/en/iqaa/mudawwar.php; maqamworld.com/en/iqaa.php (Mudawwar Shami 10/4)

name: Muhajjar
desc: A long 14/4 muwashah iqa' (sometimes grouped as a Mudawwar relative) very popular in the muwashah genre, with DUM clusters and spaced taks.
source: maqamworld.com/en/iqaa/muhajjar.php; alsiadi.com/Iqaa_Muhajjar14_4.html

name: Murabba
desc: A 13/4 muwashah iqa' ('squared') mostly confined to the muwashah repertoire, an extended cycle of DUMs and taks roughly equal to two maqsums plus a beat.
source: maqamworld.com/en/iqaa/murabbaa.php; khafif.com/rhy ('Murrabba'); maqamworld.com/en/iqaa.php (Murabba' 13/4)

name: Mukhammas
desc: A grand 16/4 muwashah iqa' ('fivefold') used in classical vocal suites, with DUMs marking the principal divisions and taks filling between.
source: maqamworld.com/en/iqaa.php (Mukhammas 16/4); maqamworld.com/en/form/vocal_comp.php

name: Dharafat
desc: A 13/8 muwashah iqa' with an irregular limping division, anchoring DUMs against syncopated taks in the classical vocal repertoire.
source: maqamworld.com/en/iqaa/dharafat.php; maqamworld.com/en/iqaa.php (Dharafat 13/8)

name: Awis
desc: An 11/8 muwashah iqa' with an asymmetric limping feel, used in classical Arabic vocal composition.
source: maqamworld.com/en/iqaa.php ('Awis 11/8)

name: Fakhit
desc: An expansive 20/4 muwashah iqa' used in long classical vocal suites, with DUM clusters and taks distributed over the very long cycle.
source: maqamworld.com/en/iqaa.php (Fakhit 20/4); maqamworld.com/en/form/vocal_comp.php

name: Awfar Masri
desc: A 19/4 Egyptian muwashah iqa' ('most abundant'), one of the longest cycles in the classical repertoire with sparse DUM and tak anchors.
source: maqamworld.com/en/iqaa.php (Awfar Masri 19/4)

name: Khosh Rang
desc: A 17/8 Persian-named muwashah iqa' ('beautiful color') with an irregular long cycle of DUM and tak anchors used in art music.
source: maqamworld.com/en/iqaa.php (Khosh Rang 17/8)

name: Chobi (Iraqi Dabke)
desc: Iraqi dabke groove characterized by three DUMs clustered at the start of the bar (DUM DUM DUM - tak - tak), driving the line dance.
source: suhaila.com/rhythms ('Chobi/Iraqi Debke - three doums at measure beginning'); ancient-future.com

name: Daboukeh (Dabke 6/8)
desc: A 6/8 Levantine dabke rhythm (DUM tak DUM tak tak) propelling Lebanese, Syrian and Palestinian line dances with a stamping lilt.
source: ancient-future.com (Debke 6/8); Carmine Guida Cheat Sheet 'Moroccan 6 / Reng' 6/8 family

name: Zar
desc: The Egyptian/Sudanese trance-ceremony rhythm (related to Ayyub) used to drive away spirits and induce trance: DUM - - DUM tak, building in intensity.
source: babayagamusic.com ('Zar - 2/4 trance, identical time-pattern to Ayyub'); Wikipedia Dumbek rhythms

name: Zar Sudani (Mandaza/Rangaha)
desc: Sudanese zar trance rhythm (mandaza/rangaha style) in a rolling 6/8-against-12 feel, with insistent paired DUM-tak cells repeated to induce trance.
source: babayagamusic.com; Hossam Ramzy 'Sabla Tolo' Sudanese zar repertoire; ethnographic zar literature

name: Laz (7/8 dabke)
desc: A 7/8 dance rhythm grouped 2+2+3 (DUM - tak - DUM tak), known across Anatolia and the Levant for fast line dances.
source: Carmine Guida Cheat Sheet 'Laz D k T k D k k' (7/8 = 2+2+3); babayagamusic.com

name: Karsilama
desc: A Turkish 9/8 greeting dance grouped 2+2+2+3 (DUM tak DUM tak tak), staple of Roman and Anatolian dance and used in Arabic-Turkish fusion.
source: Carmine Guida Cheat Sheet 'Karsilama D T D T T' (9/8); babayagamusic.com
